title: Asymmetric 34/92nm Seeded 22-Layer Stack with SA→L-BFGS Hybrid Optimization
scientific_hypothesis: Initializing high-index (odd) layers at 34nm and low-index (even) layers at 92nm, then applying simulated annealing for global basin exploration followed by L-BFGS for local refinement, will converge to a thickness configuration that improves upon the 0.9783 baseline by better exploiting the dispersion-shifted asymmetric design space.
design_principle: Quarter-wave baseline initialization at 550nm produces symmetric 57/96nm pairs; the observed optimal displacements from iteration_26 suggest an asymmetric 34/92nm ratio better balances the dual-band spectral requirements at 45° oblique incidence.
proposed_topology: 22-layer alternating stack: Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica substrate. Total finite layers: 22.
manufacturing_considerations: thickness bounds [20, 180] nm for physical realizability
simulated annealing cooling schedule for first 5 epochs
L-BFGS line-search tolerance 1e-5 for final convergence
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack initialization provides physically motivated starting point for local optimization
Hybrid global-local optimization strategy balances exploration and exploitation in multimodal thickness space
expected_advantages: Asymmetric seed targets proven optimal displacement region from iteration_26
SA phase avoids local minima in early epochs
L-BFGS phase provides precise convergence to basin optimum
known_risks: SA cooling schedule may be too aggressive or too conservative for this specific landscape
L-BFGS may not converge if SA phase does not reach basin attraction region
22-layer count may limit achievable bandwidth compared to 24-layer alternative
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer alternating TiO2/SiO2 dielectric stack on fused silica substrate at 45° incidence. Initialize odd-indexed TiO2 layers at 34nm and even-indexed SiO2 layers at 92nm. Apply simulated annealing optimizer for epochs 1-5 with exponential cooling schedule, then switch to L-BFGS optimizer with 1e-5 line-search tolerance for epochs 6-20. Thickness bounds: [20, 180] nm for all layers. Evaluate target score using mean reflectance in 450-650nm band and mean transmittance in 700-1000nm band with equal weighting. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates, tightest_margin, thicknesses_nm for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 450-650 nm, 700-1000 nm. soft objectives: high reflectance in 450-650 nm; high transmittance in 700-1000 nm; minimized crosstalk between bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 450-650 nm; reflectance in 700-1000 nm. manufacturing constraints: maximum 24 layers.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive to replace current initialization with dispersion-shifted asymmetric seed (34/92nm) and hybrid SA→L-BFGS optimization strategy, targeting the proven optimal displacement region from iteration_26.
